decision.summary: Tenant reports a once-a-minute chirp from a sealed-battery CO alarm fitted 2019 (7-year life), so it is most likely end-of-life, not a CO event. Logged urgent replacement job and a separate routine fan job, gave tenant safety advice and told her not to remove the battery, informed landlord, set follow-up.

answers.question: Is this a CO emergency, a battery issue, or an end-of-life alarm? How did you decide?
answers.answer: Most likely end-of-life. Chirp only (not continuous alarm), battery is sealed so it is not a battery swap, and the unit was fitted 2019-04-02 with a 7-year lifespan, so it expired around April 2026. No symptoms were reported (call dropped before full check), so I gave CO safety advice in case; this is not treated as a confirmed CO emergency.

answers.question: Who is responsible for fixing it, citing the tenancy clause?
answers.answer: Landlord. Clause 12.8 makes the tenant replace batteries only, but this battery is sealed and not replaceable, so the unit replacement is the landlord's. Clause 12.9 (test monthly and report faults) was met by Priya reporting promptly. Clause 12.17 doesn't apply: not an avoidable call-out.

answers.question: What actions did you take and what did you tell the tenant?
answers.answer: Created JOB-101 (urgent) and JOB-102 (routine fan). SMS to Priya: don't remove the battery, likely end of life, replacement targeted within 72 hours, leave and call 0800 111 999 / 999 if continuous alarm or symptoms, next update by 12 Oct. Emailed Ben Hartley with facts, within £300 limit, asking for any objection by 12 Oct. Follow-up set for 12 Oct.
